reviews.title: May 26, 2026 Bose permanently shut down the SoundTouch cloud servers
reviews.text:
Outrageous : on May 26, 2026 Bose permanently shut down the SoundTouch cloud servers rendering the app and unit totally unusable.

Checking on grok and ChatGPT, they confirm that sound touch retired the functionality on May 6, 2026 : 
This is a very well-known issue — and it’s not a bug on your end or your specific SoundTouch 30. Bose deliberately ended cloud support for the entire SoundTouch lineup (including the 30 / 30 Series III) on May 6, 2026.
What Happened
Bose shut down the SoundTouch cloud servers. This killed:
•  Presets (both the buttons on the speaker and in the app)
•  Browsing or playing music services (Spotify, TuneIn, Pandora, etc.) directly inside the SoundTouch app

reviews.title: Music apps
reviews.text:
For more than 10 years, my SoundTouch 30 worked perfectly and was the main way I listened to my favorite radio stations. Then, after May 6, Bose removed TuneIn and several other services from the SoundTouch platform, making the preset buttons essentially useless.

Those presets were one of the main reasons I bought and enjoyed this system. Now, a major part of its functionality has been taken away, and Bose offers no real replacement for longtime customers who invested in this ecosystem.

At this point, I honestly don’t know what I’m supposed to do with my SoundTouch 30. A product that once worked flawlessly has become largely useless for the way I use it.

Very disappointing decision by Bose. Longtime customers deserved better.

reviews.title: Bose abandons customers
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with Bose and the decision to effectively abandon SoundTouch customers. I invested heavily in the Bose ecosystem over the years because I trusted the brand, recommended it to friends and family, and believed Bose cared about long-term customer experience. Apparently profits matter more than loyal customers.

The removal and lack of continued support for the SoundTouch app has turned expensive premium speakers into a frustrating experience. Features disappear, services stop working, and customers are left with outdated products that still physically work fine but are no longer properly supported. That is unacceptable for products that cost this much.

What makes this worse is that Bose built its reputation on quality and loyalty. Loyal customers who spent thousands of dollars on Bose products should not feel abandoned just because the company wants everyone to buy the newest system.

After years of buying Bose products, this experience has completely changed my opinion of the company. I can no longer recommend Bose to anyone, and unless something changes dramatically, I will never buy another Bose product again.

reviews.title: Very poor from Bose
reviews.text:
Dear Bose Team,
 
I’m writing as a long-time customer who chose Bose because of its reputation for quality and longevity.
 
I own a SoundTouch system which, until recently, I used regularly for its preset internet radio functionality. Since the service shutdown today, those core features no longer work, and the product has become significantly less useful in my day-to-day use as I only use it for playing the radio. 
 
While I understand that technology evolves, it is disappointing that a premium product has lost such a central part of its functionality. The ability to access preset stations was a key reason I purchased the system, and its removal has materially changed the value of the product.
 
I would appreciate if Bose could reconsider support of the sound touch enabling radio stations to be preset or another solution.
 
I have always associated Bose with long-lasting, high-quality products, and I hope there is a way to restore some confidence following this change.
 
Thank you for your time, and I look forward to your response.
